Status: A restricted inequality is proved below. The full Erdős #99 problem remains open.

I obtain an original-all-label boundary inequality stronger than the requested linear lower bound, relative to any fixed unit triangular lattice. It requires neither a selected contact core nor a positive-stress assumption.

The second, necessary part of the assignment—turning these boundary defects into a strictly positive packing cost—does not follow. I give a precise obstruction and identify the missing theorem.

## 1. A quantitative boundary theorem

Put a0=3/2a_0=\sqrt3/2a0​=3​/2, and let P⊂R2P\subset\mathbb R^2P⊂R2 be unit-separated, triangle-free, with nnn points and diameter DDD. Suppose

n≥πD24a0+D600+1.(1)n\ge \frac{\pi D^2}{4a_0}+\frac D{600}+1. \tag{1}n≥4a0​πD2​+600D​+1.(1)

Let K=conv⁡(P)K=\operatorname{conv}(P)K=conv(P). For any translated or rotated unit triangular lattice Λ\LambdaΛ, define

B10(P,Λ)=#{p∈P∖Λ:dist⁡(p,∂K)<10}.B_{10}(P,\Lambda)= \#\{p\in P\setminus\Lambda: \operatorname{dist}(p,\partial K)<10\}.B10​(P,Λ)=#{p∈P∖Λ:dist(p,∂K)<10}.

Theorem. For every D≥106D\ge10^6D≥106,

B10(P,Λ)≥2D.(2)\boxed{B_{10}(P,\Lambda)\ge2D.} \tag{2}B10​(P,Λ)≥2D.​(2)

The conclusion holds uniformly over all translations and rotations of Λ\LambdaΛ, and counts original physical points, not selected-core vertices.

This theorem is conditional only on the explicitly stated separation, triangle-freeness, diameter and population assumptions. Global optimality enters solely through the known population reserve (1).

The argument combines Oler's finite-packing inequality with a partition of the triangular lattice into disjoint unit equilateral triples.

Nw≥(πwa0−π2+1600)D−πw2a0+πw.(3)\boxed{ N_w\ge \left(\frac{\pi w}{a_0}-\frac\pi2+\frac1{600}\right)D -\frac{\pi w^2}{a_0}+\pi w. } \tag{3}Nw​≥(a0​πw​−2π​+6001​)D−a0​πw2​+πw.​(3)

The sublattice

## 3. Why this does not produce the required packing cost

The theorem establishes a substantial all-label defect count. It does not establish that such defects waste packing area.

Here is a rigorous obstruction to charging a universal positive cost based on triangle-freeness and the population reserve alone.

Let PPP be an actual global minimizer of diameter D=D(n)D=D(n)D=D(n). For every ε>0\varepsilon>0ε>0, construct

Pε=(1+ε)P.P_\varepsilon=(1+\varepsilon)P.Pε​=(1+ε)P.

Then:

- All pairwise distances exceed 1, so PεP_\varepsilonPε​ is triangle-free.
- Its cardinality remains exactly nnn.
- Its diameter is Dε=(1+ε)DD_\varepsilon=(1+\varepsilon)DDε​=(1+ε)D, arbitrarily close to D(n)D(n)D(n).

g(P)≥γD−D5−60,γ=0.001939936045…,g(P)\ge \gamma D-\frac{\sqrt D}{5}-60, \qquad \gamma=0.001939936045\ldots,g(P)≥γD−5D​​−60,γ=0.001939936045…,

whose right-hand side is strictly greater than D/600D/600D/600 for D≥106D\ge10^6D≥106. If this stronger reported estimate is accepted, continuity ensures that sufficiently small positive ε\varepsilonε preserves

n−1−πDε24a0≥Dε600.n-1-\frac{\pi D_\varepsilon^2}{4a_0} \ge\frac{D_\varepsilon}{600}.n−1−4a0​πDε2​​≥600Dε​​.

Thus PεP_\varepsilonPε​ satisfies every hypothesis of the boundary theorem, including the population reserve, and has at least 2Dε2D_\varepsilon2Dε​ off-triangular-lattice boundary-strip points for every unit triangular lattice.

Yet

Dε−D(n)=εDD_\varepsilon-D(n)=\varepsilon DDε​−D(n)=εD

can be made arbitrarily small.

This disproves any proposed uniform positive diameter-gap inequality based only on triangle-freeness, the reserve, and the boundary-defect count.

It does not disprove Erdős #99: PεP_\varepsilonPε​ is not an exact diameter minimizer.

There is a second obstruction. For generators of length 1 meeting at angle

θ=π3+δ,δ>0,\theta=\frac\pi3+\delta,\qquad \delta>0,θ=3π​+δ,δ>0,

the corresponding rhombic lattice has no unit equilateral triangle, while its covolume is

sin⁡θ=a0+δ2+O(δ2).\sin\theta=a_0+\frac{\delta}{2}+O(\delta^2).sinθ=a0​+2δ​+O(δ2).

Taking δ=o(1/D)\delta=o(1/D)δ=o(1/D) makes the bulk density loss o(D)o(D)o(D) in a diameter-DDD region. Hence triangle-freeness alone cannot enforce a positive linear density penalty. This is a geometric countermodel, not a global-optimality counterexample.

## 4. Exact missing step

The established conclusions now include two different kinds of linear information:

1. The selected-positive-contact-core analysis yields η/D≥0.6099043189−o(1)\eta/D\ge0.6099043189-o(1)η/D≥0.6099043189−o(1), with its stated transfer to the original joint-MAX stress support GGG.
2. The proof above gives at least 2D2D2D original off-triangular-lattice labels within distance 10 of the original hull boundary.

There is no demonstrated incidence relation between these two sets of objects. In particular, the off-lattice labels need not belong to GGG, and the diameter branching cannot be charged to them individually.

The missing theorem is an exact-optimality-sensitive boundary-capacity obstruction. One sufficient form would be an independently established inequality, valid for every sufficiently large triangle-free global minimizer,

n−1≤πD24a0+cD+o(D),c<1600.(7)n-1\le\frac{\pi D^2}{4a_0}+cD+o(D), \qquad c<\frac1{600}. \tag{7}n−1≤4a0​πD2​+cD+o(D),c<6001​.(7)

Alternatively, a protected, same-nnn, strictly smaller-diameter competitor would close the argument.

Neither follows from (2), the selected-core branching bounds, or the current Type-I/Type-II reductions. The near-equilateral rhombic example shows why an individual off-lattice point cannot automatically carry a fixed positive cost.
